```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Made-up data for this demo, don't reuse it thinking it's real.

pacman::p_load(rio, tidyverse, janitor)
```

# Wide to long

```{r}
wide <- rio::import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx")

head(wide, 10)
```

```{r}
# names_to and values_to are just what you want the two new columns called
long <- wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = wk40:wk47, names_to = "week", values_to = "cases")

head(long, 12)
```

```{r}
nrow(wide)
nrow(long) # same numbers, just stacked
```

# Why long

```{r}
# this is why you go long. ggplot wants x, y, and color each as its own column
# just the big counties, 93 lines is a mess
long %>%
  filter(region == "Large") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = cases, color = county, group = county)) +
  geom_line()
```

# Back to wide

```{r}
long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = week, values_from = cases) %>%
  head()
```

# Crosstab

```{r}
# which = picks the sheet. leave it off and you get the first one
linelist <- rio::import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx", which = "flu_linelist")

head(linelist)
```

```{r}
# count then widen, that's your crosstab
linelist %>%
  count(county, sex) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n)
```

```{r}
# NA just means no rows to count. values_fill = 0 turns it into an actual zero
linelist %>%
  count(county, sex) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  adorn_totals(c("row", "col"))
```

# Filling blanks

```{r}
# Excel exports do this, county only on the first row of each block
export <- rio::import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx", which = "flu_export")

export
```

```{r}
# fill() copies the last value down until it hits the next one
export %>%
  fill(county)
```
